binders: Universally quantify a natural number m, including m = 0; its Lean binder is implicit.
Universally quantify a function q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ^m, represented in curried form by q x t i.
Universally quantify a matrix A = coefficient ∈ ℝ^{m×m}, with rows and columns indexed by 0, …, m−1.
Universally quantify x ∈ ℝ and t ∈ ℝ.
On the right side of the equivalence, existentially quantify qt ∈ ℝ^m, then qx ∈ ℝ^m. These witnesses are chosen within the scope of m, q, A, x and t; qx is also within the scope of qt.
The bound variables τ and ξ range over all real numbers in the slices τ ↦ q(x,τ) and ξ ↦ q(ξ,t), respectively.
hypotheses: There are no additional hypotheses on m, q, A, x or t beyond their types. The real algebraic and topological structures and finite index enumeration are supplied instances.
conclusions: LocalDef001(q,A,x,t) holds if and only if there exist vectors qt and qx such that τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative qt at τ = t, ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative qx at ξ = x, and qt + A qx = 0.
The equation means that for every i with 0 ≤ i < m, qt_i + Σ_{j=0}^{m−1} A_ij qx_j = 0.
Both implications are asserted. After unfolding LocalDef001 and LocalDef002, the left and right propositions are identical.
mathematical_definitions: ℝ^m is the space of functions Fin m → ℝ, with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication and the product topology of the usual real topology.
A_ij = coefficient i j, and (A v)_i = Σ_{j=0}^{m−1} A_ij v_j; vectors are multiplied on the left by A.
The zero vector is the function i ↦ 0.
The time-slice derivative assertion means lim_{h→0, h≠0} (q(x,t+h) − q(x,t))/h = qt in ℝ^m.
The space-slice derivative assertion means lim_{h→0, h≠0} (q(x+h,t) − q(x,t))/h = qx in ℝ^m.
LocalDef002 is precisely the existence of those two slice derivatives with qt + A qx = 0, defined for any finite coordinate type. LocalDef001 abbreviates its specialization to Fin m.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every nonnegative integer m, every real m-component function q of two real variables, every real m-by-m matrix A, and every real point (x,t), the predicate LocalDef001(q,A,x,t) is equivalent to the following condition: both partial derivatives of q at (x,t) exist as vector-valued ordinary real derivatives, and ∂q/∂t(x,t) + A ∂q/∂x(x,t) = 0. More explicitly, there are vectors qt and qx that are respectively the derivatives at t of τ ↦ q(x,τ) and at x of ξ ↦ q(ξ,t), and their sum qt + A qx is the zero vector. The predicate on the left is defined by this same condition, so the proposition is a definitional characterization.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: There is no requirement that m be positive. When m = 0, the vector space and matrix type each have one element, both slices are constant into the one-element vector space, and the derivative and equation condition holds automatically; there are no coordinate equations.
The function is defined on all of ℝ × ℝ. Derivatives are unrestricted two-sided derivatives, not one-sided derivatives or derivatives relative to a spatial or temporal domain.
The condition concerns one supplied point (x,t). Universal quantification of x and t makes the equivalence valid at every point, but does not assert that q satisfies the condition at every point.
Existence of the two partial derivatives is part of the defined condition, not an unconditional consequence for every q. If either derivative fails to exist, both sides of the equivalence are false.
No joint differentiability, joint continuity, continuous partial derivatives, or neighborhood regularity of q is required.
A is a single real matrix parameter, with no dependence on x or t in its type. No symmetry, invertibility, diagonalizability, eigenvalue condition or hyperbolicity assumption is present.
The proposition supplies no initial conditions, boundary conditions, evolution formula, or existence or uniqueness result for solutions q.
The derivative witnesses are chosen for the particular parameter tuple; no globally defined derivative fields or regularity of witness choices are asserted.

The variable names suggest spatial and temporal roles, but the formal condition only distinguishes the first and second real arguments and imposes no physical interpretation or nonnegative-time restriction.
